items.q: Look! A whale ______ right next to our boat!
items.vi: Nhìn kìa! Một con cá voi đang bơi ngay cạnh thuyền của chúng ta!
items.explanation: Look! means the action is happening at this very moment, so the present continuous is swimming is needed. ✗ swims — present simple is for habits and facts, not an action in progress now; ✗ swam — past simple puts the action in the finished past, but the whale is here now; ✗ has swum — present perfect gives a completed result, not something we are watching happen.

items.q: Lan ______ the early bus to the beach because she woke up late.
items.vi: Lan lỡ chuyến xe buýt sớm ra biển vì cô ấy dậy muộn.
items.explanation: You miss a bus, train or plane when you arrive too late to catch it, and woke up late is the clue. ✗ lost — you lose an object, a match or your way, not a vehicle you failed to catch; ✗ failed — you fail an exam or fail to do something; a bus cannot be its object; ✗ dropped — to let something fall from your hands.

items.q: The boat trip was cancelled because of ______ winds along the coast.
items.vi: Chuyến đi thuyền bị hủy vì gió mạnh dọc bờ biển.
items.explanation: Wind that blows with great force is strong wind; the clue is that it was powerful enough to cancel the boat trip. ✗ heavy — collocates with rain, snow and traffic, not wind; ✗ hard — describes work, questions or a hard frost, never wind; ✗ big — used for size (a big wave), not for the force of wind.

items.q: The hotel was lovely, and the free boat trip to the island was ______.
items.vi: Khách sạn rất đẹp, và chuyến đi thuyền miễn phí ra đảo là phần thưởng tuyệt vời thêm vào.
items.explanation: The icing on the cake is an extra good thing that makes an already good situation (the hotel was lovely) even better. ✗ the tip of the iceberg — a small visible part of a much bigger problem; ✗ a piece of cake — something very easy to do; ✗ the last straw — the final problem that makes you lose patience, the opposite of good news.

items.q: Let's stay inside the tent until the storm ______.
items.vi: Chúng ta hãy ở trong lều cho đến khi cơn bão qua đi.
items.explanation: A storm or an argument blows over when it passes and things return to normal; stay inside until shows we are waiting for it to end. ✗ blows up — explodes, or suddenly loses its temper; ✗ blows out — puts out a candle or flame with a breath; ✗ breaks down — a car or machine stops working, or a person starts crying.

items.q: The dog ______ the gate open by itself; it was locked all night.
items.vi: Con chó không thể nào tự đẩy cổng mở được; cổng đã bị khóa suốt đêm.
items.explanation: Can't have + past participle is a confident deduction that something did NOT happen; the clue it was locked all night makes it impossible. ✗ mustn't have pushed — 'must have' is for positive deductions only; its negative is 'can't have'; ✗ shouldn't have pushed — criticises something that really happened; ✗ needn't have pushed — says it was done but was unnecessary.

items.q: The whole class passed the chemistry test, ______ the teacher very proud.
items.vi: Cả lớp đều đậu bài kiểm tra Hóa, điều đó khiến cô giáo rất tự hào.
items.explanation: After a comma, which can refer back to the WHOLE clause before it (the fact that everyone passed), so , which made is right. ✗ that made — 'that' cannot start a non-defining clause after a comma; ✗ what made — 'what' means 'the thing that' and cannot refer back to a clause; ✗ who made — 'who' is for people, and no person is the antecedent here.

items.q: Our school team ______ the visitors 3–1 in the final of the eco-quiz.
items.vi: Đội trường mình đã thắng đội khách 3–1 trong trận chung kết cuộc thi đố vui về môi trường.
items.explanation: You beat an opponent, and the object here is the visitors (the other team). ✗ won — you win a match, a game or a prize, not the other team; ✗ gained — you gain experience, weight or confidence, never an opponent; ✗ achieved — you achieve a goal or success, never a team.

items.q: By next summer, my family ______ every beach in Da Nang.
items.vi: Đến mùa hè năm sau, gia đình tôi sẽ đi hết mọi bãi biển ở Đà Nẵng.
items.explanation: By next summer marks a deadline in the future, and an action finished before that deadline takes the future perfect will have visited. ✗ will visit — simple future says only that it happens later, not that it is complete by then; ✗ has visited — present perfect links to now, not to a future point; ✗ is visiting — an action in progress, not one finished.

items.q: Don't worry about lunch – Mum has packed ______ sandwiches for the whole group.
items.vi: Đừng lo về bữa trưa – mẹ đã gói rất nhiều bánh mì kẹp cho cả nhóm rồi.
items.explanation: Plenty of (more than enough) is used with BOTH plural countable nouns like sandwiches and uncountable nouns. ✗ much — only with uncountable nouns (much food), and mainly in negatives and questions; ✗ a great deal of — only with uncountable nouns (a great deal of time); ✗ a large amount of — only with uncountable nouns; countable plurals take 'a large number of'.

items.q: Before our trip to Australia, Dad spent every evening ______ his English.
items.vi: Trước chuyến đi Úc, bố dành mỗi tối để ôn lại tiếng Anh.
items.explanation: Spend + time + -ing is a fixed pattern, so spent every evening brushing up on (improving his rusty English) is right. ✗ to brush up on — 'spend time' never takes a to-infinitive; ✗ brush up on — a bare verb cannot follow the noun 'evening'; ✗ brushed up on — a second past tense would need 'and' to join it to 'spent'.

items.q: We ______ hundreds of photos of the elephants at the sanctuary.
items.vi: Chúng tôi đã chụp hàng trăm bức ảnh về những con voi ở khu bảo tồn.
items.explanation: The English collocation is take a photo, so took hundreds of photos is right. ✗ made — you make a cake or a decision; 'make a photo' is a direct-translation error; ✗ did — 'do' goes with homework, the shopping or a job, not photos; ✗ caught — you catch a ball, a bus or a cold, not a photo.

items.q: The zoo's plan to breed rare parrots ended in ______ when none of the eggs hatched.
items.vi: Kế hoạch nhân giống vẹt quý hiếm của sở thú đã thất bại khi không quả trứng nào nở.
items.explanation: A plan that does not reach its aim ends in failure; the clue is none of the eggs hatched. ✗ defeat — being beaten by an opponent in a contest or war, but the zoo was not competing; ✗ loss — losing something you had (a loss of money), not a plan that did not work; ✗ mistake — a wrong action or choice, not the result of a plan.

items.q: Living in the city centre is exciting; ______, the rent costs a fortune.
items.vi: Sống ở trung tâm thành phố rất thú vị; mặt khác, tiền thuê nhà thì đắt khủng khiếp.
items.explanation: On the other hand introduces the opposite side of a situation: exciting BUT the rent costs a fortune. ✗ in addition — adds a similar point, but expensive rent is a contrast, not another plus; ✗ as a result — shows a consequence, and high rent is not caused by excitement; ✗ for instance — gives an example of the previous point, not a disadvantage.

items.q: Choosing where to go on holiday usually ______ how much money you have.
items.vi: Việc chọn đi nghỉ ở đâu thường quy về chuyện bạn có bao nhiêu tiền.
items.explanation: Something boils down to one thing when that thing is the real deciding factor, here how much money you have. ✗ boils over — liquid rises and spills from a pan, or anger explodes; it also has no 'to' for the object; ✗ breaks down — stops working, or is divided into parts; ✗ puts up with — tolerates something unpleasant.

items.q: You ______ bring a tent; the campsite lends them to visitors for free.
items.vi: Bạn không cần mang lều; khu cắm trại cho khách mượn miễn phí.
items.explanation: Needn't means it is not necessary, and the reason the campsite lends them for free shows a tent is unnecessary, not forbidden. ✗ mustn't — a prohibition (you are not allowed to), which the sentence does not give; ✗ can't — impossibility or 'not allowed', but bringing a tent is possible; ✗ shouldn't — advice that it is a bad idea, not a lack of need.

items.q: My family ______ in this fishing village since my grandfather was a boy.
items.vi: Gia đình tôi đã sống ở làng chài này từ khi ông tôi còn là một cậu bé.
items.explanation: Since + a past starting point (my grandfather was a boy) for a situation still true now takes the present perfect have lived. ✗ live — present simple gives no link to the past starting point; ✗ lived — past simple would mean the family no longer lives there; ✗ are living — present continuous describes now only and does not go with 'since'.

items.q: Lan wishes she ______ her camera to the bird park yesterday.
items.vi: Lan ước gì hôm qua cô ấy đã mang máy ảnh đến công viên chim.
items.explanation: A regret about the past (yesterday) uses wish + past perfect, so had brought is right. ✗ brought — wish + past simple is for a present situation we want to be different, not a finished past event; ✗ has brought — the present perfect is never used after 'wish'; ✗ would bring — wish + would complains about someone else's future behaviour, not a past regret.

items.q: It took the campers three ______ to light the fire in the wet forest.
items.vi: Những người cắm trại phải thử đến ba lần mới nhóm được lửa trong khu rừng ẩm ướt.
items.explanation: An attempt is one act of trying, so you can count three attempts before success. ✗ efforts — effort is the energy you put in; 'three efforts' does not count tries; ✗ trials — a scientific experiment or a court case, not a try at lighting a fire; ✗ tests — a check of knowledge or quality, not an act of trying.

items.q: The beach ______ we camped last year is now closed to protect the sea turtles.
items.vi: Bãi biển nơi chúng tôi cắm trại năm ngoái nay đã đóng cửa để bảo vệ rùa biển.
items.explanation: Where replaces a place adverb: we camped there (on the beach), so no preposition is needed. ✗ which — would need a preposition ('on which we camped') because 'camp' takes no object; ✗ that — same problem: 'that we camped' leaves the verb with nothing to do; ✗ whom — only for people as an object, never for a place.

items.q: The showers at the campsite were not ______, so we complained to the owner.
items.vi: Nhà tắm ở khu cắm trại không đạt yêu cầu, nên chúng tôi đã phàn nàn với chủ khu.
items.explanation: Up to scratch means of an acceptable standard; the clue is that the showers were bad enough to complain about. ✗ up in the air — still undecided (used of plans); ✗ up in arms — very angry and protesting; a person is up in arms, not a shower; ✗ under the weather — slightly ill, used of people.

items.q: ______ had we reached the campsite when it began to pour with rain.
items.vi: Chúng tôi vừa mới tới khu cắm trại thì trời bắt đầu mưa như trút nước.
items.explanation: Hardly + had + subject + past participle ... when means the second event followed the first immediately; the clue is when after the comma. ✗ No sooner — also takes inversion but pairs with 'than', not 'when'; ✗ Not until — the inversion comes in the MAIN clause after the time clause ('Not until we arrived did it rain'), not straight after these words; ✗ Only when — same pattern: 'Only when we arrived did it rain'.

items.q: The guide told us to ______ a close eye on our bags at the night market.
items.vi: Hướng dẫn viên bảo chúng tôi để mắt kỹ tới túi xách của mình ở chợ đêm.
items.explanation: The fixed expression is keep an eye on something (watch it carefully), so keep a close eye on our bags is right. ✗ hold — you hold a bag or a hand, but there is no idiom 'hold an eye on'; ✗ take — 'take a look at' exists, but 'take an eye on' does not; ✗ put — you put something somewhere; there is no idiom with 'eye on'.

items.q: Mai ______ her passport twice before she finally found it in her coat pocket.
items.vi: Mai đã kiểm tra hộ chiếu hai lần trước khi cuối cùng tìm thấy nó trong túi áo khoác.
items.explanation: The checking happened before another past action (before she finally found it), so the earlier action takes the past perfect had checked. ✗ has checked — present perfect links to now and cannot sit with a finished past clause; ✗ checks — present simple is for habits, not a past story; ✗ is checking — an action in progress now, not one before a past event.

items.q: The baby turtle ______ to reach the sea before the seagulls noticed it.
items.vi: Chú rùa con đã tìm được cách ra tới biển trước khi lũ mòng biển phát hiện.
items.explanation: Manage to + verb means to succeed in doing something difficult, and the to-infinitive to reach is the clue. ✗ succeeded — needs 'in + -ing' (succeeded in reaching), never a to-infinitive; ✗ achieved — takes a noun object (achieve a goal), not to + verb; ✗ reached — already means 'arrive at' and takes a place as object; 'reached to reach' repeats itself.
